disclaimer: Advisory only: these recommendations support a human analyst. They are generated from a model prediction that can be wrong, and this system does not block, filter, or prevent any traffic.

actions.action: Ask the upstream provider / DDoS-protection service to filter the volumetric traffic before it reaches the IoT network.
Apply per-source and per-protocol rate limits on the edge router or firewall for the targeted destination.
If the flooding sources are devices inside the network, move them to a quarantine VLAN.
Track packets/s and bytes/s per destination against the normal baseline and keep a packet capture for investigation.
Identify the single offending source address and block or rate-limit it at the firewall.
Enable connection limits and shorter timeouts on the targeted service or device.
Monitor CPU, memory and connection-table usage of the targeted device to confirm recovery.
Isolate the participating IoT device(s) from the network; reboot and restore firmware before reconnecting (Mirai spreads by guessing default Telnet/SSH passwords [18]).
Replace factory-default credentials on all IoT devices with unique strong passwords.
Disable Telnet and other unused remote-administration services on IoT devices.
actions.mitigation_name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

actions.action: Update device firmware to a version that fixes known weaknesses.
Filter the outbound flood at the egress firewall so infected devices cannot attack others.
Raise the scanning source on the watch list and correlate it with later alerts — scans often precede an attack.
Close unused ports and disable services the device does not need, to shrink what a scan can find.
actions.mitigation_name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

actions.action: Keep IoT devices in a separate network segment so a scanner cannot reach everything.
Enable IDS/IPS signatures for port-scan, host-discovery and OS-fingerprinting patterns.
Enable Dynamic ARP Inspection and DHCP snooping on the switches serving the IoT devices.
Use static ARP entries for critical hosts such as the gateway.
actions.mitigation_name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

actions.action: Point devices to trusted DNS resolvers that validate DNSSEC, and verify recent DNS answers.
Prefer encrypted device communication (TLS) so intercepted traffic is not readable.
Enable IDS/IPS rules for adversary-in-the-middle traffic patterns.

Web-based.title: Web application attack (SQLi, command injection, XSS, upload, backdoor)

actions.action: Put a web application firewall / input validation in front of device web interfaces.
Patch the device firmware or web application.
Make administrative web interfaces reachable only from the management network.
actions.mitigation_name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network

actions.action: Review web-server logs for injection payloads and run a vulnerability scan of the device.
Enable account lockout or progressive delays after repeated failed logins.
Enable multi-factor authentication where the device or service supports it.
Replace weak or default passwords; use key-based authentication for SSH.
Monitor the failed-login rate per source and block sources that exceed it.
No defensive action recommended; continue normal monitoring.
Do not apply category-specific countermeasures yet: the model is not confident about this window.
Inspect the source/destination hosts and keep a packet capture of the related traffic.
Compare the evidence features and the top-2 candidate categories, then decide manually.
No category-specific playbook exists for this label; follow the general incident-response procedure.
Escalate to an analyst and record the new category so a playbook can be written.

ICMP flood.action: Rate-limit or drop ICMP echo requests at the network edge for the targeted hosts.

UDP flood.action: Rate-limit UDP traffic to the target and block UDP ports the device does not use.

TCP SYN flood.action: Enable SYN-flood protection (SYN cookies / SYN proxy) and shorten the half-open connection timeout.

TCP flag/connection flood.action: Use stateful filtering to drop TCP packets that do not belong to an established connection (RST/FIN/PSH-ACK floods).

HTTP/application-layer flood.action: Place a reverse proxy or web application firewall in front of the device web service with request-rate limits and short idle timeouts (also mitigates slow-request attacks such as Slowloris).

GRE-encapsulated flood.action: Drop GRE (IP protocol 47) traffic at the edge if the network does not use GRE tunnels.
